Chapter 06 of 19

The Old Line

East Van / erased rail routes
The story

Vancouver has taken a lot of routes off its maps: streetcar rails, rail spurs, stops that used to matter. Terminal City has not. The Old Line is the city's memory, buried in its infrastructure, and on wet nights it shows itself. Look into a puddle on a street with no tracks and you may see rails shining in the reflection.

The Old Line does not run on a timetable, and it does not care what the current map says. It exists so the city is never trapped inside the present. Old alignments, old rights-of-way, old versions of a corner keep feeding into the new build, and a car on the Old Line might stop where a place used to matter rather than where a passenger expects.

The Repair People mark remembered places along it. The crows inspect it. The 3:17 Freight shares its rails but does the opposite job: the Freight removes what cannot stay, and the Old Line keeps what must not be forgotten. You may follow an old route. You may not assume it goes where the current map says.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
